inlines.text: Using the area of a rectangle, write a formula for the area of the kite.

answer.worked:
The rearranged rectangle has width $x$ and height $y/2$.
$$\begin{align*}A&=x\times\frac{y}{2}\\A&=\frac{xy}{2}\end{align*}$$

inlines.text: Why is a rhombus also a kite?
A rhombus has four equal sides, meaning its
sides are equal. So, it’s a kite.

answer.worked: A rhombus has four equal sides, so it has two pairs of equal adjacent sides. Therefore, it is a kite.

inlines.text: Why is a rhombus also a parallelogram?
A rhombus has two pairs of
sides, meaning it’s a parallelogram.

answer.worked: Both pairs of opposite sides of a rhombus are parallel. Therefore, it is a parallelogram.

answer.worked:
The parallelogram has base $a+b$ and perpendicular height $h$.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{two trapeziums}}&=\text{base}\times\text{perpendicular height}\\A_{\text{two trapeziums}}&=(a+b)h\\A_{\text{two trapeziums}}&=h(a+b)\end{align*}$$

children.prompt: Therefore, what is the area of a trapezium?

answer.worked:
The two congruent trapeziums have equal areas, so one has half the parallelogram’s area.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{trapezium}}&=\frac{A_{\text{two trapeziums}}}{2}\\A_{\text{trapezium}}&=\frac{h(a+b)}{2}\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:
Convert the rectangle height: $0.8\text{ m}=80\text{ cm}$. The top semicircle has radius $60\div2=30\text{ cm}$.

A_{\text{bottom trapezium}}&=\frac{5(64+60)}{2}\\
A_{\text{bottom trapezium}}&=310\text{ cm}^2\\
A_{\text{middle rectangle}}&=80\times60\\
A_{\text{middle rectangle}}&=4800\text{ cm}^2\\
A_{\text{top semicircle}}&=\frac{\pi(30)^2}{2}\\
A_{\text{top semicircle}}&=450\pi\text{ cm}^2\\
A_{\text{hole}}&=\pi(20)^2\\
A_{\text{hole}}&=400\pi\text{ cm}^2\\
A_{\text{remaining}}&=310+4800+450\pi-400\pi\\
A_{\text{remaining}}&=5110+50\pi\text{ cm}^2\\
A_{\text{remaining}}&\approx5267.1\text{ cm}^2
\end{align*}$$

The remaining area is $5267.1\text{ cm}^2$, correct to one decimal place.

spec.description: Tall unfilled triangle with apex slightly right of its left base endpoint. Sloping sides are labelled t and n. A dashed perpendicular height divides the horizontal base into e and 4e, with a right-angle marker at its foot.
spec.mathematics: Height 85 mm; base segments e and 4e. The two right triangles determine t and n after e is found from the total area.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown labels appear; calculated lengths remain in answer fields.

answer.short: $e=12.0\text{ mm},\quad t=85.8\text{ mm},\quad n=97.6\text{ mm}$. Use $2550=\frac{85\times5e}{2}$ to find $e$, then apply Pythagoras to each right triangle.
answer.worked:
The total base is $e+4e=5e$. Use the triangle-area formula, then Pythagoras in each right triangle.
$$\begin{align*}
2550&=\frac{85\times5e}{2}\\
2550&=\frac{425}{2}e\\
e&=12\text{ mm}\\
4e&=48\text{ mm}\\
t^{2}&=12^{2}+85^{2}\\
t&=\sqrt{7369}\text{ mm}\\
t&\approx85.8\text{ mm}\\
n^{2}&=48^{2}+85^{2}\\
n&=\sqrt{9529}\text{ mm}\\
n&\approx97.6\text{ mm}
\end{align*}$$
Thus $e=12.0\text{ mm}$ to 1 d.p.

Using Pythagoras’ theorem in each right triangle:

entries.description: a. Identify the special quadrilateral shown.

Right-leaning parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides. Opposite sides have matching parallel-arrow markings and matching equality-tick sets; the two opposite-side pairs use distinct markings.
b. Identify the special quadrilateral shown.
Trapezium with a shorter horizontal top side and longer horizontal bottom side. Matching arrows mark those parallel sides. One equality tick on each sloping side marks equal nonparallel sides.
c. Identify the special quadrilateral shown.
Upright kite with a longer lower point. The two sides meeting at the top have single equality ticks; the two sides meeting at the bottom have double equality ticks. No parallel arrows.
d. Identify the special quadrilateral shown.
Diamond-oriented rhombus. All four sides have the same equality-tick marking. Opposite-side pairs have matching parallel arrows, with distinct arrow sets for the two pairs.
e. Identify the special quadrilateral shown.
Wide, shallow rhombus with its long diagonal horizontal. All four sides have matching equality ticks. Opposite-side pairs have matching parallel-arrow sets.
f. Identify the special quadrilateral shown.

Parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides and sloping sides descending to the right. Opposite sides carry matching parallel arrows and equality-tick sets; the two pairs use distinct markings.
g. Identify the special quadrilateral shown.

Trapezium with horizontal parallel sides, a vertical right side and a sloping left side. The bottom side is longer than the top. Matching arrows mark the horizontal sides; no equality ticks or right-angle marker.
h. Identify the special quadrilateral shown.
Horizontally oriented kite with its longer point to the right. The two sides meeting at the left vertex have single ticks; the two meeting at the right vertex have double ticks. No parallel arrows.
i. Identify the special quadrilateral shown.
Tall, narrow upright kite. The two sides meeting at the top have single equality ticks; the two meeting at the bottom have double equality ticks. No parallel arrows.
j. Identify the special quadrilateral shown.
Trapezium with a shorter horizontal top side, longer horizontal bottom side and two differently inclined sloping sides. Matching arrows mark the horizontal parallel sides. No equality ticks.
k. Identify the special quadrilateral shown.

Wide, shallow parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides and slightly inclined lateral sides. Opposite sides carry matching parallel arrows and equality-tick sets; the two pairs use distinct markings.
l. Identify the special quadrilateral shown.
Broad diamond-oriented rhombus. All four sides have matching equality ticks. Opposite-side pairs have matching parallel arrows, with distinct arrow sets for the two pairs.
m. Identify the special quadrilateral shown.
Trapezium with a shorter horizontal top side and longer horizontal bottom side. Matching arrows mark those parallel sides. Both lateral sides slope outward towards the bottom; no equality ticks.
n. Identify the special quadrilateral shown.
Tall, narrow diamond-oriented rhombus. All four sides have matching equality ticks. Opposite-side pairs have matching parallel-arrow sets.
o. Identify the special quadrilateral shown.
Wide upright kite with a pronounced upper point and shallow lower point. The two upper sides have single equality ticks; the two lower sides have double equality ticks. No parallel arrows.
p. Identify the special quadrilateral shown.
Right-leaning parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides. Opposite sides carry matching parallel arrows and equality-tick sets; the horizontal and sloping pairs use distinct markings.
q. Identify the special quadrilateral shown.
Wide, right-leaning parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides. Opposite sides carry matching parallel arrows and equality-tick sets; the two pairs use distinct markings.
r. Identify the special quadrilateral shown.
Tall, narrow upright kite. The two sides meeting at the top have single equality ticks; the two meeting at the bottom have double equality ticks. No parallel arrows.
s. Identify the special quadrilateral shown.
Very wide, shallow rhombus with its long diagonal horizontal. All four sides have matching equality ticks. Opposite-side pairs have matching parallel-arrow sets.
t. Identify the special quadrilateral shown.
Trapezium with a longer horizontal top side and shorter horizontal bottom side. Matching arrows mark those parallel sides. Both lateral sides slope inward towards the bottom; no equality ticks.

Since the adjacent sides are equal, a rhombus is also a kite.
The opposite sides are parallel, so a rhombus is also a parallelogram.
